title: [3.13] gh-140594: Fix an out of bounds read when feeding NUL byte to PyOS_StdioReadline() (GH-140910) (#145853)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow in PyOS_StdioReadline (myreadline.c:345) in a 100-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.
allocator_layer: libc malloc (the object never reaches a pymalloc pool)
layer_note: measured: the heap report SURVIVES PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc, so the object is not a pymalloc block. It is PyMem_RawMalloc d (myreadline.c:207,223,325,347) -- a libc block at 100 bytes, which is why the <=512 B shortcut was wrong

spatial.oracle: a fault at the offending access: cause 5 on a load or 7 on a store where the access leaves the object's own capability, or cause 24 where it reaches memory the system allocator has already freed and revoked. The object is a system allocator block, so one of the two applies; completion would falsify this. The fault must carry cause 5, 7 or 24; any other cause, cause 2 (ILLEGAL_INST) among them, is an ordinary trap rather than this arm's mechanism and falsifies this.
spatial.oracle_premise: Corrected at review, 2026-10-10: the premise that this arm revokes is false. Its level0 heap only marks a freed block free (capstone/ports/musl-capstone/runtime/level0.c, l0_free), patch 0009 issues no revoke, and the runtime's only revoke sites release thread context areas, reached only through __clone; so nothing on this arm revokes heap memory. A cause 24 here is UNEXP_OP_TYPE, an access through an untagged base register: a pointer slot that later data overwrote (tag integrity), or an integer or NULL used as a pointer -- not revocation. The oracle above is kept as written; see results/20261006/README.md, 'Corrections made at review'.

sublet.oracle: fault: the object is a libc malloc block

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: the arm does not separate this case, and the admissible outcomes are stated rather than one of them predicted: si_code=1 (PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS) where the access goes beyond the bounds the allocator actually set, si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG) where it instead lands in memory a revocation sweep has already reclaimed, or completion where it stays inside the bounds the allocator set -- malloc may bound a capability to a rounded size class rather than the requested length. The mechanism is live and the run proves it rather than assuming it: mech-control S_OOB faults with si_code=1. Any other si_code would falsify this.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial DETECTED cause=5 (spatial-20261007-020747); sublet DETECTED cause=5 (sublet-20261007-022142); cheribsd-revocation DETECTED si_code=1 (boundary-20261008-075318)
